title: Swap the tray on a passing cart in one pass, without stopping it
instruction: A cart with a full tray in its nest is passing in front of you and won't stop. Take the full tray off the cart and set it on the grey outfeed table, and put the empty tray from the stand into the cart's nest before the cart reaches the red line.
context: On assembly lines and at AGV transfer points, carts and pallet carriers bring trays of parts past a station that must swap the full tray for an empty one while the carrier keeps moving, because stopping it would stop the line; both trays have to be handled within the one pass, so the unload and the reload must be coordinated and matched to the cart's motion. Done by: line-side material handlers and robot cells at tray-exchange points.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table (110 x 130 cm). A black track bed (18 cm wide, 124 cm long, 1 cm tall, ending 3 cm inside each table edge) runs across the table from the right to the left, parallel to the line through the arm bases, its centre 33 cm in front of it. A grey aluminium cart (18 x 18 cm, 4 cm tall) rides on it, 2 mm above the bed, square to it, its centre starting 53 cm to the right of the midpoint between the bases; its top is 5.2 cm above the table. On the cart's top stands a nest: a lead-in funnel of four black steel guide plates (2.4 cm wide, 0.4 cm thick, 13.3 cm long), one along each side of a square pocket 13.5 x 13.5 cm centred on the cart, each leaning outward at 55 degrees from the horizontal with its inner lower edge on the pocket's edge, 3 mm above the cart, so the pocket widens to 16.3 x 16.3 cm at the funnel's top, 2.3 cm above the cart; the plates stand 1 mm apart at the corners. Two identical blue polypropylene trays (150 g each): square, 11 x 11 cm outside, 3.5 cm tall, 0.5 cm walls and floor, with a yellow handle rib (1.2 cm thick, 10 cm long) across the middle of the inside, running perpendicular to the track, whose top is 7.5 cm above the tray's underside (4 cm above the rim); the rib splits the tray into two compartments 4.4 cm wide. The full tray sits in the middle of the nest, its rib perpendicular to the track, with a bare aluminium block (6 x 3 x 2 cm, 100 g) lying flat in the middle of each compartment, its long side along the rib. The empty tray sits centred on a grey stand (a box 15 x 15 x 3 cm) whose centre is 14 cm in front of the bases and 37 cm to the left of the midpoint, rib perpendicular to the track. An identical grey box, the outfeed table, stands 14 cm in front of the bases and 37 cm to the right of the midpoint, empty. Two strips of red tape (6 x 1.2 cm) mark the end line across the table on both sides of the bed, 46 cm to the left of the midpoint, 0.5 cm from the bed. Nothing else is on the table. The cart starts with the trial: it speeds up from rest to 6 cm/s in 0.5 s and runs on at that speed without stopping; its centre passes in front of the right arm base 4.0 s into the trial, in front of the left arm base 14.2 s in, and reaches the end line 16.75 s in. Past the table's left edge the track turns down and takes the cart out of reach.
scoring: Two halves of 0.5 each. The nest is judged once, when the cart's centre reaches the end line: 0.5 if the empty tray is then seated in the nest (its centre within 1.5 cm, horizontally, of the cart's centre, its underside within 5 mm of the cart's top, level within 5 degrees, moving with the cart within 2 cm/s) and let go (both grippers' grasp points, between the fingers, 5 cm or more from the middle of the tray's rib, 2.75 cm above its rim); 0.25 if it is then let go and riding on the cart but not seated (its centre over the cart's top, its underside within 3 cm above it, for example perched on a guide plate); otherwise 0. A tray placed after the cart passed the line doesn't count, and what happens after the line doesn't change this half. The full tray is judged at the end of the trial: 0.5 if it rests on the outfeed table (its centre over the table's top, its underside within 1 cm of it, level within 10 degrees, still) with both blocks inside it (each block's centre between the tray's walls, above its floor and below its rim) and let go; 0.25 if at some point it was taken off the cart (its underside 4 cm or more above the cart's top) and at the end it is level within 10 degrees with both blocks inside it, off the cart, but not set down on the outfeed table and let go (for example still held, or set on the bare table); otherwise 0 (left on the cart, dropped, tipped, or a block spilled). Score: the sum (0 to 1.0); 1.0 when both halves score 0.5, and the trial then ends with success once that has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Stop the track, put the cart back at its start with the full tray (both blocks in it) in its nest and the empty tray on the stand, clear the outfeed table, and start the cart with the trial. Catch anything that leaves on the cart past the table's edge.
fidelity: The cart and its guide plates follow their path exactly, like a stiff servo-driven carrier on a guide track: the arms can't push, stop or tip it. The cart floats 2 mm above the bed and past the table's edge moves straight down. Each tray is one rigid body of six boxes (floor, four walls, handle rib), friction 0.8/0.7; the blocks have the station's rubber-like friction (1.2/1.0). The cart's acceleration (under 0.2 m/s², only in its first 0.5 s) can't slide a tray or a block.
